summary: White Rock lookout, Douglas County, OR: cabin built 1917-1919, D-6 cupola cabin 1923, lightning damage 1931, removed 1967 or 1970; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Cabin with an open-air cupola, replaced in 1923 by a D-6 cupola cabin (register)
facts.status_note: Removed in 1970 per the register and destroyed that year per firelookout.com; Forest Lookouts gives 1967 for removal. No source describes the site today.

visit.trail_note: A three-mile trail from South Myrtle to the station was completed in 1917 (Forest Lookouts quoting a newspaper). No source describes access to the site today.

events.note: Construction of the station building under way in September 1917 (Forest Lookouts quoting the Riddle Tribune); the register gives 1919
Cabin with an open-air cupola built (register and firelookout.com)
D-6 cupola cabin replaced the 1919 cabin; Forest Lookouts quotes an August 1923 report of knocked-down buildings shipped to the site
Lookout reported 25 to 30 incendiary fires on the divide between North and South Myrtle creeks
Ground house with a 7-by-7 cupola constructed (Forest Lookouts)
Neil Tripp at the White Rock lookout station; away a few days through illness in July
Report of vandalism turned out to be lightning damage; 15 of 18 windows broken
Army deactivated the White Rock AWS station
Forest Lookouts: lookout discontinued and removed
Register: removed in 1970; firelookout.com: destroyed in 1970

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts quotes a September 1917 report of construction under way; the register and firelookout.com give 1919 for the first cabin. Not reconciled; the story gives both.
The register and firelookout.com say 1970; Forest Lookouts says discontinued and removed in 1967. Not reconciled; the story gives both.
The register gives 4,019 ft (1,225 m); a January 1931 Douglas County report gives 4010 feet. The record keeps 1,225 m from the register.

notes_for_editor: Building history is contradictory: 1917 construction, 1919 first cabin (register), 1923 replacement, then a 1926 log cabin and 1928 ground house in Forest Lookouts; the story says the history is unclear. Removal is 1967 (Forest Lookouts) or 1970 (register, firelookout.com). Brief height_m 3.0 has no source. Two searches found nothing describing the site today. Forest Lookouts quotes both 4,010 ft (1931) and the register's 4,019 ft. No photos added. The 1931 lightning story in Forest Lookouts is a real event at the lookout, not a fire.
